newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIAN INSTITUTE SEES FURTHER RAPID ECONOMIC GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIAN INSTITUTE SEES FURTHER RAPID ECONOMIC GROWTH.

text.p: The Estonian Institute for Market Research said on Thursday that it estimated GDP would grow by six percent in 1997 and 1998.

"The growth in the economy, which started in the third quarter of 1996 has continued, reaching six to seven percent in the first half-year according to previous estimates," the institute added in a booklet published on Thursday.
Estonia's GDP grew by 4.9 in the third quarter and by 7.3 percent in the fourth quarter last year.
The institute added that other statistical figures such as exports, industrial sales, average wages and retail turnover indicated high activity in the economy.
The institute said that the overall local economic situation in six months would be as favourable as it is now.
Some 52 percent of its experts estimated the situation would stay stable in six months while 24 percent thought the situation would be better in six months.
The estimate is based on positive changes in industry, which enable exports to rise and reduce the current account deficit.

Some 24 percent of experts estimated the situation would worsen because of high inflation and possible import restrictions, which would reduce competitiveness and worsen its image for foreign investors.
